providers.name: Claude Code
providers.rollback: The setup command only prints Claude hook JSON; it does not change ~/.claude/settings.json. If you manually merged the generated hook entries there, remove only AgentTrace's commands while retaining other hooks.
providers.privacy: Events pass through AgentTrace's normal redaction path; hook visibility is limited to fields emitted by the provider.
known_gaps: PostToolUseFailure sends no tool_response and no separate exit code: the failure text is in a top-level error field, and for a Bash command it starts with the exit code ("Exit code 1") followed by the command's error output. agent-strace records that text, cut to 500 characters, as the error event's text. is_interrupt is not recorded, so an error event does not say whether the user interrupted the call; no call was interrupted in the recording.
SessionStart carries no model name and no hook reports the session's token usage, so session_start has an empty model and sessions record no tokens.

SubagentStart and SubagentStop fire in the parent session but setup does not register them, so no subagent_start or subagent_stop events are recorded. A subagent's tool calls arrive under the parent session_id and are recorded in the parent trace with its agent_id and agent_type, between the parent's Agent tool_call and tool_result.

A tool denied at the permission prompt (in claude -p, any call without an --allowedTools grant) fires PreToolUse and PermissionRequest but no post hook, so its tool_call has no result or error. PermissionRequest is not registered.
File and command activity is visible only in tool arguments and results: Bash calls carry tool_input.command, Read, Edit and Write carry tool_input.file_path, and no file_write events are recorded.

providers.name: OpenAI Codex
providers.rollback: Setup preserves the original bytes once at hooks.json.agent-strace.bak next to $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json (default ~/.codex/hooks.json) before overwriting an existing file. Restore them with cp ~/.codex/hooks.json.agent-strace.bak ~/.codex/hooks.json, replacing ~/.codex with "$CODEX_HOME" when it is set. If no file existed before setup, remove the generated hooks.json from that directory instead.
providers.privacy: Events pass through AgentTrace's normal redaction path; hook visibility is limited to fields emitted by the provider.
known_gaps: The setup command replaces hooks.json rather than merging; repeated runs retain the first hooks.json.agent-strace.bak snapshot.
Codex runs command hooks only after they are reviewed and trusted in /hooks; codex exec skips untrusted hooks without a warning. Hooks added by a later setup run must be trusted again.
SessionEnd always reports reason "other", so the session_end event does not say why the session ended.

Subagents are not separate sessions: their hooks arrive under the parent session_id with an agent_id. SubagentStart and SubagentStop are recorded as subagent_start and subagent_stop events in the parent trace, and the subagent's tool events carry its agent_id and agent_type, but no event links a subagent to the spawn_agent call that started it.
A failed shell command arrives as a normal PostToolUse with the error text in tool_response and no exit code, so it is recorded as a tool_result rather than an error.

Token usage comes only from PostModelRequest, which Codex 0.164.0 and later fire after every model request, including a subagent's. Each is recorded as an llm_response event with the model, status, error and token_usage; a subagent's also carry its agent_id and agent_type. In token_usage, input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens, output_tokens includes reasoning_output_tokens, and total_tokens is their sum. PreModelRequest is not registered, so no llm_request event is recorded: llm_response events have no parent_id and no request duration. A failed or cancelled request is an llm_response with that status and no token usage, not an error event. Older Codex releases record no token usage.
File and command detail depends on PreToolUse/PostToolUse payloads; shell calls arrive as tool_name Bash with tool_input.command.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
providers.rollback: Setup writes a dedicated file and leaves other Copilot hook files unchanged. Remove it with rm ~/.copilot/hooks/agent-strace.json, using $COPILOT_HOME/hooks/agent-strace.json when COPILOT_HOME is set. If you installed the agent-strace Copilot CLI plugin instead, run copilot plugin uninstall agent-strace.
providers.privacy: Events pass through AgentTrace's normal redaction path; hook visibility is limited to fields emitted by the provider.
known_gaps: A main session's trace may begin with its first user_prompt event. 1.0.94-3 fired userPromptSubmitted before sessionStart and 1.0.103-0 did so in some runs. 1.0.107 fired sessionStart first, but userPromptSubmitted followed within milliseconds without waiting for the sessionStart hook to finish, so in 4 of 5 recorded non-interactive runs the user_prompt event was written first.

Subagents started with the task tool record prompt, tool and stop events under their own session id with no session_start and no session_end. The parent's subagentStop hook (and subagentStart in 1.0.107 and some 1.0.103-0 runs) names the child, so the parent records subagent_start and subagent_stop events and the child's meta.json is linked to the parent. Subagent hooks carry no tool call id, so the link to the parent's task tool_call is set only when exactly one task call is pending. Sessions captured before these hooks were registered stay unlinked; re-run agent-strace setup --cli copilot or update the plugin to register them.
agentStop carries a stop reason and transcript path but no response text, so stop events have empty text.
Hook payloads carry no model name or token usage.
From 1.0.107, tool hooks carry toolCallId; it is recorded as tool_use_id and pairs each result or error with its call. Earlier versions send no call id, so results are paired with calls by tool name.
A shell command that exits non-zero is reported through postToolUse with resultType success, so it is recorded as a tool_result; the exit code appears only in the result text.

A tool denied at the permission prompt leaves its tool_call without a result or error; the permissionRequest and notification hooks that report it are not registered. permissionRequest also fires for tools granted with --allow-tool.
userPromptTransformed (the prompt as sent to the model, with a prepended current_datetime block), preCompact and errorOccurred hooks are not registered.
File and command activity is visible only in tool arguments and results; no file_write events are recorded.
Stores written before agent-strace 0.97.0 have no meta.json for subagent sessions; run agent-strace backfill-meta --apply to make them visible.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
providers.rollback: Delete .github/hooks/agent-strace.json and .github/hooks/agent-strace-cloud.sh from the default branch, then remove the AGENT_STRACE_ENDPOINT and AGENT_STRACE_AUTH_KEY Agents secrets and the collector firewall allow rule.
captured_signals: The job prompt, at most once per job (userPromptSubmitted)
Tool calls with tool name and arguments (preToolUse)
Session end with reason complete, error, or timeout (sessionEnd)
not_captured_signals: errorOccurred, userPromptTransformed, and preCompact events, which fire in cloud agent but are not registered
permissionRequest and notification events, which do not fire in cloud agent
Setup steps, firewall blocks, and other job log output that does not pass through a hook
Any event recorded while AGENT_STRACE_ENDPOINT is unset or the collector is unreachable; it is discarded with the sandbox
Every event of a job in which agent-strace is not on PATH and the one-time install fails
Links between sessions of separate jobs on the same pull request; each job is recorded as its own session
Workflow artifact or pull request attachment upload
providers.privacy: By default, events are redacted before they leave the sandbox, then sent to the collector named by the AGENT_STRACE_ENDPOINT Agents secret. Agents secrets are readable by the agent, so the collector key must guard nothing else.
known_gaps: Not verified in a live cloud agent job. The template follows the documented hooks reference, and tests run the generated script locally against hook payloads and an authenticated collector.
Hook output written in the sandbox is discarded when the job ends. Events survive only when they are streamed to an agent-strace server collector that the cloud agent firewall allows.
Uploading the trace as a workflow artifact or pull request attachment is not supported: GitHub documents no token or upload step that runs after the agent and before the sandbox ends.
agentStop carries a stop reason but no response text, so stop events have empty text.
Hook payloads carry no model name or token usage.
Copilot CLI tool hooks carry toolCallId only from 1.0.107; without it, tool results are paired with calls by tool name.
File and command activity is visible only in tool arguments and results; no file_write events are recorded.
Recorded sessions name the github-copilot agent, so health and evidence reports apply the GitHub Copilot CLI matrix entry rather than this one.
